title: Fix: HttpExecutor/ToolRunner raise TypeError for a rendered body holding an integer beyond 64 bits
description: va_common.json.dumps (orjson) raises 'Integer exceeds 64-bit range'; HttpExecutor.execute (dumps(call.body)) and ToolRunner._capped/excerpt (dumps_str) let it escape although both promise never to raise. Reachable only through a stored tool/webhook-node/dynamic-data body literal with such an integer (model arguments arrive as JSON text and orjson parses big ints as floats). Probes: logs/probe_plan_t03.py, logs/probe_plan_t03b.py. Dynamic data (P08-T03a) is shielded by the fetcher's own boundary; tools and webhook nodes are not.

title: Fix: a number beyond 64 bits in a call's JSONB (variables, metadata, request_data) may break webhook body serialization
description: Found while reviewing P08-T03a (not caused by it). Verified: a float >= ~1.8e19 (e.g. 1e20, 3.4e38) written to a jsonb column comes back from Postgres as a Python int beyond 64 bits (probe logs/probe_review2_t03a_db_test.py: calls.variables {'blob': 340282366920938500000000000000000000000} for a context float 3.4e38); orjson.dumps of such an int raises TypeError 'Integer exceeds 64-bit range'. va_events.webhook_delivery.Deliverer.send does orjson.dumps(delivery.payload) (webhook_delivery.py:191) and va_events.model.encode uses va_common.json.dumps. NOT verified end to end: whether a Call Object with such a variable/metadata value reaches a delivery payload and what the dispatcher does with the TypeError. Reachable without dynamic data (Send Call metadata {"x": 1e20}). First write a failing test (seed a call with metadata_ {'x': 10**20}, run emit_completed + one dispatcher run_once), then fix in ONE place (serializer or the JSONB read), same family as fix:http-body-big-int.
